sources: Air India / Air India Express travel advisory on X, Oct 30, quoted verbatim by News18, Business Today, Mathrubhumi, CNBC-TV18, NDTV
fault_line: Airlines now price the Saudi air war to mid-November -- does a two-week suspension mean the attacks are expected to continue, or just caution?

sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- airline's own advisory, quoted verbatim] 'Due to the prevailing situation in the region, Air India and Air India Express flights to and from Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam will remain suspended until 14 November 2026 (inclusive).' Passengers with bookings issued on/before Oct 30 for travel up to Nov 14 may rebook once free (travel up to Nov 29) or take a full refund. [VERIFIED FACT -- prior baseline] Oct 24 advisory had set Riyadh/Dammam suspensions until Nov 7 and Jeddah until Oct 31 -- so Jeddah is extended 14 days, Riyadh/Dammam 7 days. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- other carriers] IndiGo cancelled Jeddah/Dammam/Madinah until Nov 14; Akasa Air suspended Riyadh until Nov 30 and Jeddah until Nov 10 (via Business Today/CNBC-TV18). The suspension is attributed by outlets to Ansar Allah attacks on Saudi airports/energy sites; the airline advisory itself cites only 'the prevailing situation'.
sections.what_verified: No publisher family with a declared tier in the registry carries this item (News18, Business Today, Mathrubhumi, CNBC-TV18, NDTV all unregistered) -- so family_count is 0 by the registry rule, even though five outlets quote the airline's X post verbatim. Sig is 2, so the sig>=3 two-family gate is not triggered; if production treats this as sig-3 it must be HELD pending a tiered source or the airline post itself.
sections.what_disputed: None on the dates -- all relays agree verbatim. The causal link to Ansar Allah attacks is outlet attribution, not the airline's stated reason ('prevailing situation'). No Saudi aviation-authority statement retrieved.
sections.why_matters: The Saudi air war, measured in departure boards: Air India just pushed its Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam suspension to November 14 -- Jeddah was supposed to reopen on October 31.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Oct 30, absent from Oct 30/31 scans) -- Air India + Air India Express extend Saudi flight suspension (Jeddah, Riyadh, Dammam) until Nov 14 inclusive; IndiGo to Nov 14, Akasa Riyadh to Nov 30

totw_analysis: Our read: The Saudi air war, measured in departure boards: Air India just pushed its Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam suspension to November 14 -- Jeddah was supposed to reopen on October 31. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Airlines now price the Saudi air war to mid-November -- does a two-week suspension mean the attacks are expected to continue, or just caution?
